saa-med-313.text: A company needs to decide between transferring 80 TB by the internet (dedicated link of 500 Mbps, usable ~50% for this task) or use a AWS Snowball Edge (total time limit) ~1 the week between shipment, copy and return). 80 TB a 250 Effective Mbps take about 30 days, what is the recommendation and the main criterion?
options: Internet, because dedicated links are always more reliable
DataSync on the internet, because it compresses the data and would reduce the deadline to hours
Snowball Edge, because when the network transfer would take more than ~1 week, the physical device tends to be faster and cheaper
Split data into several bucks to speed up the link
saa-med-313.explanation: A) Incorrect: reliability does not change the band's mathematics — 30 days against 1 week. B) Incorrect: DataSync optimizes and parallels, but does not perform miracle with the physical band; compression does not reduce 30 days to hours. C) Correct: the pocket rule of the AWS: if the network transfer takes more than ~1 week, use the Snow family — 80 TB fit in a single Snowball Edge. D) Incorrect: split into buckets does not increase the available band of the link.

saa-med-314.text: What is the central difference between AWS DataSync and the AWS Storage Gateway?
options: DataSync is for TRANSFERIR/migrate data (one-time or scheduled) between on-premises and AWS; Storage Gateway provides CONTINU HYBRID access, with local cache and cloud data
Storage Gateway transfer faster than the DataSync in any scenario
DataSync only works with relational databases
They are the same service with names from different generations
saa-med-314.explanation: A) Correct: this is the classic distinction of proof — DataSync moves data from A to B (with integrity check and scheduling); Storage Gateway integrates the cloud datacenter permanently (File/Volume/Tape Gateway with local cache). B) Incorrect: they are different purposes; speed is not the criterion of choice. C) Incorrect: DataSync transfer ARQUIVOS/objects (NFS, SMB, HDFS, S3, EFS, FSx); banks are the territory of DMS. D) Incorrect: separate and complementary services.

saa-med-315.text: A company makes corporate backups in physical tapes (tape library) with legacy software and wants to eliminate the management of physical tapes and transport to external vaults, maintaining the same backup software. AWS replace the tapes with the minimum of changes?
options: Migrate all backups to the Amazon EBS
AWS Storage Gateway — Tape Gateway, featuring a VTL (Virtual Tape Library) to backup software, with virtual tapes in S3/S3 Glacier
AWS Backup with centralized plans
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
saa-med-315.explanation: A) Incorrect: EBS is block disk for EC2 — expensive and inadequate for backup archiving. B) Correct: The Tape Gateway emulates a tape library (VTL) compatible with existing backup software; tapes have seen objects in S3 and file in S3 Glacier — zero change in backup flow. C) Incorrect: AWS Backup orchestrate backups of RECURSOS AWS, does not replace the tape interface of the on-premises legacy software. D) Incorrect: FSx is a server file, not related to tape libraries.

saa-med-316.text: Business partners send files daily via SFTP. The company wants to receive these files directly in a pocket S3, maintaining the protocol SFTP for partners (without changing anything), without managing servers. Which service meets this scenario?
options: AWS Transfer Family with endpoint SFTP integrated with S3
Enable SFTP natively in the pocket S3
Amazon EC2 with an OpenSSH server and cron synchronization
AWS DataSync with agent in the partner
saa-med-316.explanation: (a) Correct: or Transfer Family provides SFTP/FTPS/FTP fully managed, with files falling directly into S3 (or EFS) — partners continue to use the same client SFTP. B) Incorrect: or S3 Don't talk. SFTP native. C) Incorrect: works, but violates the requirement not to manage servers. D) Incorrect: DataSync requires agent and is for transfers between storages, not to receive uploads SFTP of third parties.

saa-med-317.text: A company will migrate to the AWS a Windows server file that uses the protocol SMB and is integrated with Microsoft Active Directory (permissions) NTFS, DFS). Windows applications should continue to access sharing without change. Which storage service is appropriate?
options: Amazon EFS
Amazon S3 with AWS Transfer Family
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
Amazon EBS with Multi-Attach
saa-med-317.explanation: (a) Incorrect: EFS It's NFS (Linux world) — does not offer SMB or integration with NTFS/AD.B) Incorrect: S3 is storage of objects; is not a file server SMB. C) Correct: FSx for Windows is the native managed Windows server file: SMB, integration with Active Directory, ACLs NTFS and DFS — transparent migration for applications.: EBS Multi-Attach is shared block for few EC2 with cluster file system, not a file server SMB.

saa-med-318.text: A workload of HPC (high-performance computing) for scientific simulations requires a file system with hundreds of GB/s throughput and submilisecond latency, processing datasets that reside in the Amazon S3. What service has been designed for this?
options: Amazon EFS in Max I/O mode
Amazon FSx for Lustre, with native integration to the buckets S3
Amazon S3 Standard with Transfer Acceleration
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
saa-med-318.explanation: (a) Incorrect: EFS Max I/O scale well, but does not reach the throughput/latence profile of HPC of Lustre. B) Correct: the FSx for Lustre is the parallel file system for HPC/ML, with native integration to S3 (load and return data from the pocket in a transparent way).: S3 is object — does not provide file system interface POSIX of very high performance for HPC. D) Incorrect: FSx for Windows handles loads SMB corporate, no HPC.

saa-med-319.text: A mobile game developer wants to run start servers with latency POUCOS MILISSEGUNDOS for connected users via network 5G of a specific operator, putting the computer of the AWS within the operator's network. Which service meets this case?
options: AWS Outposts in the developer's datacenter
AWS Wavelength, with Wavelength Networked Zones 5G of operators
Amazon CloudFront with edge locations
AWS Local Zones in another city
saa-med-319.explanation: A) Incorrect: Outposts leads to AWS for the datacenter of CLIENTE, not within the mobile operator's network. B) Correct: Wavelength implants computer/store of AWS on the edge of the nets 5G of operators, eliminating jumps to the internet — single-digit ms latency for mobile devices. C) Incorrect: CloudFront Accelerates delivery of CONTENTS via cache; does not execute start servers. D) Incorrect: Local Zones close to AWS of large urban centers, but the requirement here is to be DENTRO Network 5G.

saa-med-320.text: A media producer in a metropolis SEM Region AWS next needs to run virtual workstations and latency rendering of few milliseconds for your local artists, using the services and standard APIs of AWS, without installing hardware in the office itself. Which infrastructure option solves?
options: Create a VPC in any region and use Direct Connect
Install AWS Outposts in the office
AWS Wavelength
Use one AWS Local Zone of that metropolis, extending the VPC for her
saa-med-320.explanation: A) Incorrect: Direct Connect gives network consistency, but latency up to a distant region continues to be too high for interactive workstations. B) Incorrect: it would meet, but requires installing and hosting hardware in the office — the requirement says 'no hardware'. C) Incorrect: Wavelength is for latency via networks 5G operators, not for fixed offices. D) Correct: Local Zones are extensions of Regions in large metropolises: the VPC extends to the local area and resources (EC2, EBS) run few ms of users.

saa-med-321.text: With remote work, employees of a company need to access, from their notebooks and anywhere, internal applications hosted in private sub-networks of a VPC — with encrypted connection (TLS) and authentication integrated into the corporate directory. What service provides this access?
options: AWS Client VPN, with endpoint associated with VPC and federated/AD authentication
AWS Site-to-Site VPN in each residence
VPC Peering between the employees' houses and the VPC
Make public sub-networks with Security Groups restrictive
saa-med-321.explanation: A) Correct: the Client VPN is the VPN GERENCIADA for individual users: OpenVPN client/TLS no notebook, elastic endpoint associated with VPC and authentication via Active Directory, SAML or certificates. B) Incorrect: Site-to-Site connects REDES (office ↔ VPC), Incorrect: peering connects VPCs to each other, not people. D) Incorrect: expose private sub-networks publicly violates the basic principle of security of the scenario.

saa-med-322.text: A web application in a single instance EC2 in a single AZ suffers unavailability when the instance fails. DUAS Do combined actions make architecture highly available? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Create a Auto Scaling Group with at least 2 instances distributed in multiple AZs
Increase the size of the current instance (scale-up))
Distribute traffic with a Application Load Balancer pointing to the instances in multiple AZs
Create a AMI of the instance as backup
Move the instance to a public subnet
saa-med-322.explanation: (a) Correct: or ASG ensures the minimum number of instances and automatically replaces them (self-healing), spread by AZs. B) Incorrect: a larger instance remains a single point of failure. C) Correct: the ALB monitors health and distributes traffic only to healthy instances between AZs — the classic pair ALB + ASG multi-AZ. D) Incorrect: AMI accelerates manual recovery, but does not prevent unavailability. E) Incorrect: the public subnet does not change availability.

saa-med-323.text: A company needs to ensure that the objects of a pocket S3 are encrypted at rest with auditable keys and that TODO access to the pocket occurs only by encrypted connections. DUAS do settings implement these requirements? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Enable standard bulk encryption with SSE-KMS using a customer managed key
Enable bucket versioning
Add a condition to the bucket policy NEGUE requests when aws:SecureTransport for False
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration
Mark the bucket with compliance tags
saa-med-323.explanation: A) Correction: SSE-KMS with CMK encrypts at rest and records each use of the key in CloudTrail — B) Incorrect: versioning protects against exclusion/overwriting, no encryption or force TLS. C) Correct: the condition aws:SecureTransport=false with Deny blocks any access HTTP no TLS — the standard way to force encryption in transit. D) Incorrect: Transfer Acceleration accelerates uploads, is not security control. E) Incorrect: tags organize and rate costs; do not apply controls..

saa-med-324.text: Two microservices communicate by calls HTTP direct synchronous: when processing service is slow or unavailable, customer requests are lost. In addition, a new 'created order' event will need to activate THREE independent systems. DOIS services solve, respectively, the disconnection with buffer and the distribution of the event to multiple systems? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Amazon SQS as a line between services, absorbing peaks and unavailability of the consumer
AWS Direct Connect among microservices
Amazon SNS publishing the event for multiple subscribers (fan-out))
Amazon EBS shared between services
AWS Global Accelerator between services
saa-med-324.explanation: A) Correct: with row SQS in the middle, the producer deposits and follows; messages await the consumer to recover — nothing gets lost. B) Incorrect: Direct Connect is physical connectivity with on-premises.: SNS delivers the same registered N event (fan-out) — the default to trigger the three systems (ideally SNS → 3 rows SQS). D) Incorrect: EBS is not a mechanism for communication between services.: Global Accelerator optimizes the network path of global users, does not disconnect services.
